teaser.text: Most people meet Cadence Design Systems only indirectly: its software and machines help turn a chip idea into something a factory can build. The business earns money by selling that design capability, reusable circuit blocks and testing capacity, then spends it on engineers, suppliers and the infrastructure that keeps the work running.

stock.title: Cadence stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Cadence stock forecast: weighted scenarios, cash after stock pay, and valuation explained in plain English.
stock.opening: Cadence's weighted price is US$330.91 in October 2029, with the bear case at 30%, the base case at 55%, and the bull case at 15%. It hinges on cash growth and execution offsetting a lower valuation multiple.
stock.closing: The full Cadence memo also answers how Cadence makes money, how it compares with rivals, how management is executing, and what risks could change the case.

blocks.heading: Where could Cadence's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: Cadence’s forecast is nearly flat because operating progress is largely offset by a lower valuation multiple. The weighted price is $327.41 in October 2027, a 1% total return including dividends. It is $330.66 in October 2028, a 2% return. It is $330.91 in October 2029, also a 2% return. The final bear-to-bull range is $324.65 to $335.04, against today’s $324.38.

The bear case receives 30%. The base case receives 55%. The bull case receives 15%. The base case therefore carries the forecast, but the narrow range says execution matters more than a major re-rating.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Cadence, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base path grows cash by 10% annually. Its table values are supported by an $8.1 billion backlog, continuing renewals and strong design activity, but acquisition costs and stock compensation restrain conversion. The bear path starts at $1,050 million and grows 3% annually because weaker budgets, delivery friction and integration costs would interrupt growth. The bull path starts at $1,490 million and grows 15% annually because Q2 revenue, Core EDA and IP all showed strong momentum.

The bear case requires weaker design budgets, tougher competition, slower China deliveries and costly integration. It ends at $324.65 after starting at $324.95. Its probability is 30% because cash after stock pay has previously declined, receivables have risen, and export uncertainty remains material.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Cadence really make?

paragraphs.text: Cash from operations was 1,728,781 in 2025. After capital spending of 141,871, free cash flow was 1,586,910. This captures spending on equipment and facilities, but not every cost of staying competitive: R&D salaries already reduce operating cash flow, while acquisitions appear elsewhere.

earnings.title: Cadence earnings: guidance and next results
earnings.meta_description: Cadence expects its next results on October 26, 2026; annual guidance is in force, with backlog conversion and cash collection to watch.
earnings.opening: Cadence expects to report its next results on October 26, 2026. The key thing to watch is whether Cadence converts backlog into revenue and collects the cash implied by earnings.
earnings.closing: The full memo explains Cadence’s business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: Management’s July 27, 2026 guidance calls for 18%–20% revenue growth in 2026. It puts revenue at US$6,260,000–6,340,000 thousand. The plan includes US$2,000,000 thousand of operating cash flow and US$240,000 thousand of capital spending. Stock compensation is US$569,000 thousand.

blocks.heading: Did Cadence keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Buybacks can offset dilution, which is the spreading of ownership across more shares, but spending money on repurchases does not guarantee that dilution disappears. Management also beat its 2025 revenue and adjusted-earnings outlook while missing its forecast under standard accounting rules. Adjusted earnings remove selected costs, including stock pay and acquisition-related items; standard accounting includes them.

blocks.heading: What has Cadence reported in revenue and profit?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached 1,584,451, up approximately 24.2% from June 2025. It was also up 7.5% from March 2026. Core EDA grew 18% and IP grew more than 40%. System Design and Analysis grew 37%, although Hexagon contributed to that category.

Cash from operations was 634,929, and capital spending was 59,603. Free cash flow rose, but gross margin fell from 85.6% to 84.9%, so faster sales did not improve every layer of profitability. Backlog reached $8.1 billion, including $4.2 billion of RPO revenue expected within twelve months. The quarter supports continued expansion, not a sudden doubling of recurring operating profit.

blocks.heading: What should Cadence watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: Cadence is due to report third-quarter results on October 26, 2026. Management expects quarterly revenue of $1.595 billion to $1.625 billion and non-GAAP earnings of $2.01 to $2.07 per share. The important evidence will be whether it maintains the annual outlook, converts backlog and collects the cash implied by earnings.
